text:
sam: Heads-up — the raven-lite int8 canary we spun up this morning is showing weird funcall outputs: arrays sometimes missing the last element or have an off-by-one index shift. :thinking_face:

sam: Repro harness (minimal):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood/dev/invoke \\  -d '{"model":"raven-lite-int8","prompt":"CALL tool extract_items()","stream":true, "seed":1234}'
```

sam: Example output we logged (streamed -> assembled):
```json
{"tool":"extract_items","args":[{"id":0,"name":"foo"},{"id":1,"name":"bar"}]}
# expected third item but missing - sometimes last item appears as {"id":2,"name":"baz"} at the start of a subsequent stream chunk
```

marta: ugh. do we see this only on streaming or also non-stream?

sam: so far only on streaming. non-streamed responses look ok for same seed. suspect tokenizer boundary + kvcache prefilling interaction with PTQ kernels.

jess: could be a tokenization offset mismatch where an EOS or sentinel token gets swallowed during chunk framing. any diffs in tokenizer output between fp16 and int8 runs?

liam: can you paste the raw token ids and chunk boundaries for a failing trace? quick grep of logs should do.

sam: pasted below (trimmed):
```
chunks: [ [101, 205, 999], [400, 502, 2], [3, 4] ]
assembled tokens: [101,205,999,400,502,2,3]   # note last token 4 missing in assembled output
```

prashant: that looks like a stream-assembly race where the last fragment lost its final byte -> parse got truncated. does our stream-retry/backfill logic request the missing tail?

marta: currently we only do a retry on transport failure, not on parse-detected truncation. we could add a fast end-of-stream sanity check: if JSON parse fails, attempt a nondeterministic backfill by re-invoking with stream=false for the same request id.

jess: agreed. also add a small checksum header across chunks to detect lost bytes earlier.

canary-bot: alert: model=raven-lite-int8 canary: funcall-parse-failure rate 1.76% (baseline 0.28%) — details at https://canary.redwood/alerts/6171234567

liam: proposing action plan:
- increase canary sampling from 1% -> 5% for next 2 hours to gather more signals (liam)
- add parse-failure detection that triggers a fallback non-streamed re-invoke (marta)
- run 10k seeded replay across mirrored staging and compare token-level diffs (sam + jess)
- add per-chunk checksum and chunk-assemble debug logs for 24h (prashant)

marta: I'll own the fallback change and smoke it on staging in ~2h.

sam: I'll start the seeded replay now and drop logs into #eng-ml-results.

jess: will help analyze tokenization diffs, also check kernel selection logs for mismatched kernel paths between int8 and fp16.

prashant: one caveat — fallbacks may add latency for users when parse-failure is common. let's gate the re-invoke: only when funcall schema parse fails AND checksum indicates missing chunk.

marta: agreed. fallback only for schema-conforming calls that fail parse, and we should include an SLI to track extra latency introduced.

sam: small note — add a temporary label to canary runs to keep these traces separated from normal telem: tag=stream-parse-probe-617123

liam: I'll bump sampling and patch canary config now. ping back when you have a reproducible token-id trace and I'll spin a mirror run on the same commit/hash.

marta: thanks. if anyone hits a quick low-effort mitigation, post it here. otherwise we'll sync after the 2h smoke. :thumbsup:
